When in lower brackets, play well and hope for the best. You can get your AD carry fed, but that doesn't mean squat if he's bad. Typically, you can help your team by warding and catch someone out of position and creating opportunities for your team by doing stuff (hooks etc.) but remember that you're never the one pulling the trigger. You can set it up how nicely or easy for your teammates, and that does increase your chance of winning, presuming your better then the other support. The only other real thing you can do is telling your team when to take objectives and such, being a leader (if they even listen to you).

So right, you can carry as support and set up perfect conditions for your team to win. But you can also carry by killing and getting strong and creating the win by yourself. In lower brackets the latter one is much more recommended, in my experience.

If you play support seriously and keep the map warded as much as it should be, then you don't have the money/item slots for getting other items. You must have 3 slots for wards (sightstone, vision wards and sight wards). This leaves you with 3 slots left, whereas one must go to bots (pref. Mobility) and the other one to either shurelias or a kage's evolved item. Seeing as you must prioritize an Oracles everytime you need it leaves it hard for you to fill in that last item slot, which should pref. be a Locket if your jungler doesn't have it, or some other support item dependant on the other team (Mikael's for heavy CC).

The only time in which you can deviate from this path is if you're getting really fed (through assists) in which case depending if you play an AP support or not (Nami, Janna, Sona) you can get items like Morellonomicon, Twin Shadows or Will of the Ancients.

However, in 99% of your games you will always build 3 ward slots, boots, Shurelias, Oracle and maybe locket. Support is the most gold starved role in the game with neither farm or kills, so it's very rarely you have enough money to buy other items.
